summary: The core is laid out like a Capcom board of that era, not like MAME's exedexes driver. Sprites go through a bus-request DMA copy, then a per-line Y-match scan into a small buffer and a ping-pong line buffer. MAME's per-frame draw_sprites loop does none of this. Layer priority comes from a priority PROM addressed by each layer's opaque bits, where MAME hard-codes the draw order with pmask. The scroll layers form map-ROM addresses directly from the H/V position bits, not through MAME's tilemap scan functions, and decode palette-bank and enable registers that MAME does not model.

findings.note: A 32-entry priority PROM is addressed by {char opaque, obj prio bit, obj opaque, scr1 opaque}. Its output selects the layer mux and the palette-PROM upper bits. MAME has no such PROM: it draws bg, fg, sprites, text in a fixed order and uses a priority mask.

findings.signal: sprite DMA via Z80 bus request
findings.note: A write to C806 (OKOUT) raises BUSRQ. After BUSAK and during vblank, a counter (blen) drives the CPU RAM address lines to copy the sprite table. MAME just copies a buffer when C806 is written.

findings.signal: per-line sprite scan + double line buffer
findings.note: On each line, an adder compares the sprite Y with VF and copies up to 24 matching entries into a ping-pong buffer. Pixels are then written into one of two alternating line RAMs while the other is read out. MAME walks all 32-byte sprite entries once per frame instead.

H counts 128..511 and V reloads to 250 at the end of each frame, like a loadable counter chain. Blanking and HINIT are decoded from specific counter values, and the object LVBL runs two lines ahead for the line buffer.

findings.signal: interrupts from PROM indexed by V, synced to LHBL/H1
findings.note: The IRQ PROM is read with V[7:0]. Bit 3 is latched on the LHBL rising edge and bit 2 drives the sound interrupt on the H1 edge. The vector is built as {110,prom[1:0],111}. MAME uses the same PROM bits but fires a per-scanline timer callback with HOLD_LINE.

findings.signal: map ROM addressed directly from scroll position bits
findings.note: The tile-map ROM address is a bit concatenation of the scrolled H/V counters (e.g. {veff[10:8],heff[10:8],veff[7:4],heff[7:4]}), fetched every 8 or 16 pixels and shifted out serially. MAME expresses the same lookup as arithmetic tilemap mapper callbacks.

D806 is decoded as scroll-1/scroll-2 palette-bank latches, and the 3-bit pal_bank feeds the scroll lookup PROMs (jtexed_scr1.v:210, jtexed_scr2.v:325). MAME maps no D806 handler and fixes the tile colour banks in its palette() init.

findings.signal: lookup PROM per layer in the pixel path
findings.note: Each layer runs its pixel through its own 256x4 lookup PROM (two for sprites and scroll 2) before the mixer. The OR'd constants such as |0xc0 and |0x40 that MAME puts in palette() are absent; the mux bits come from the priority PROM instead.

The sprite engine is a parameterized module shared by several Capcom cores. The Exed Exes case only remaps attribute bits (priority bit 6, flips bits 4 and 5, X MSB bit 7), and these match MAME's draw_sprites field decode as a correct core must.
The address decode uses casez on A[15:13]/A[12:11], matching the memory map MAME lists. This is required for correctness and says nothing about provenance.
